stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Folklorists who compare stories across cultures have found that the tale of the clever fox and the vain crow is remarkably ______: versions of it have been recorded in more than forty countries, from Norway to Japan, often with only the names of the animals changed.
explanation: Skip the blank and read what comes after the colon. It says the tale appears in more than forty countries, from Norway to Japan. Summed up in one word, that is 'found in many places,' and 'widespread' says exactly that. This drill is the base skill for Words in Context questions where a colon or the next sentence defines the blank: you summarize the explanation first, then match the word to it.

B.why: You picked a word that suits folktales in general. Many folktales are old, but the text after the colon is about how many places the tale shows up, not how long ago it began. Nothing in the passage gives its age.

C.why: You matched the topic instead of the evidence. A fox tricking a crow might be funny, but the explanation after the colon counts countries. It does not describe the tone of the story.

D.why: You may have reacted to 'remarkably' without reading what followed. A tale recorded in more than forty countries is the opposite of rare.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Immunologists describe many of the body's defending cells as highly ______. A single T cell, for example, recognizes only one particular fragment of one particular virus and ignores the thousands of other molecules it encounters as it moves through the blood and tissues.
explanation: The second sentence starts with 'for example,' so it shows what the blank means. The T cell responds to one target and ignores everything else. In one word, that is 'specific.' This drill is the base skill for Words in Context questions where the sentence after the blank gives a concrete case: you name exactly the quality the example shows.

A.why: This is the trap for this question type. 'Powerful' sounds right for immune cells, but the example never says how strongly the cell attacks. It only shows how narrowly the cell chooses its target.

B.why: You went beyond the example. It describes one single T cell, so it says nothing about how many such cells the body has.

D.why: A cell that responds to only one fragment and ignores everything else is rigid in what it recognizes, not flexible. This word reverses what the example shows.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Ornithologists often call the arctic tern a remarkably ______ traveler: each year the small seabird flies from its nesting grounds in the Arctic to the coasts of Antarctica and back again, a round trip that can exceed 70,000 kilometers.
explanation: Read past the colon first. The tern flies from one end of the planet to the other, a round trip of more than 70,000 kilometers. The one idea there is distance, and 'far-ranging' names it. This drill is the base skill for Words in Context questions where a colon introduces the blank's definition: the words after the colon tell you exactly which quality to name.

A.why: This is the trap for this question type. 'Graceful' is a word people often use for seabirds, but the text after the colon gives distances and places. It never describes how the bird looks when it flies.

C.why: The passage never says whether the tern travels alone or in flocks. You added a detail the explanation does not contain.

D.why: A bird that makes a 70,000-kilometer trip every year is not reluctant to travel. This word clashes with the evidence after the colon.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Engineers designing aircraft frames often choose titanium because it is unusually ______ for a structural metal. A titanium bracket, for example, can carry the same load as a steel bracket while weighing roughly 45 percent less, which saves fuel on every flight.
explanation: The 'for example' sentence shows what the blank means. The titanium bracket does the same job as the steel one but weighs about 45 percent less. The quality being shown is low weight, so 'lightweight' is the precise match. This drill is the base skill for Words in Context questions where the next sentence defines the blank: pick the word that names what the example actually measures.

A.why: This is the trap for this question type. 'Durable' is a positive word that suits metals in general, but the example compares weight. It says nothing about how long the bracket lasts.

B.why: The fuel savings come from the lower weight, not from the price of the metal. The passage never says what titanium costs, so you assumed something it doesn't state.

C.why: The example says titanium weighs about 45 percent less than steel. 'Heavy' reverses the comparison the passage makes.
